- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to account for potential rebound.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply a “lag correction”: reduce forecast 1–3 days after peak.  
- In periods with high volatility or mean-reverting sentiment (alternating +/–), model often fails to revert; apply a “mean reversion bias” by smoothing forecast toward recent 5-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a “first-day discount” — reduce initial forecast by 3–7% to reflect diminishing confidence.  
- If sentiment history shows sustained positive sentiment with no recent negative signals, model tends to overreact; apply a “sentiment dampening” rule — reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of sustained positivity.
